data.title: Palantir Stocks Move Lower as NATO AI Sovereignty Faces Scrutiny
data.description:
Defense-AI software provider Palantir told Reuters that neither the company nor the U.S. government can remotely disable customers' Maven systems, as shares traded at $195.25, down 0.48% at 10:35 a.m. ET Friday. The statement addresses a central concern for European military buyers: who controls the technology once it is deployed?

According to Reuters' reporting, NATO purchased Maven for its European military headquarters in 2025 and declared full technical operating capability in June 2026. The platform brings together battlefield information from sources including satellites and radar. Palantir's latest reported quarterly revenue reached $1.94 billion, up 93%, with U.S. revenue rising 115% to $1.57 billion. That puts European adoption alongside an already fast-growing American business.

The valuation leaves little room for complacency. A GF Score of 83/100 sits alongside a price-to-earnings ratio of 166.31, suggesting solid business metrics come with demanding earnings expectations. Customer control addresses one technical concern, but governments still have to weigh sovereignty, security and oversight. For investors, the next meaningful signals are additional deployments, renewals and disclosed contract values. Those would show whether NATO's adoption translates into a broader European business.

data.title: US, Canadian Oil Rig Counts Rise as Crude Prices Continue to Climb — OPIS
data.description:
The number of oil rigs operating in the United States and Canada resumed its upward trajectory this week, with the U.S. count seeing its seventh increase in the past eight weeks, according to data Friday from oilfield services firm Baker Hughes.

The U.S. oil rig count rose by one during the week to 460. The count had fallen by three in the previous week. There are now 40 more rigs operating than there were at this time last year, the Baker Hughes data show. The previous week's decline could have been due, in part, to Hurricane Isaias's impact on drilling operations in the Gulf of Mexico region.

The U.S. gas rig count fell by one to 132, which is 11 more than were operating a year ago, the data show.

The Canadian gas rig count remained unchanged at 65, four more than were operating at this time last year. The oil rig count rose by two to 152, 14 more than were in operation a year ago, according to Baker Hughes.

Rig counts are considered a leading indicator of oilfield activity. The rise in the oil rig counts comes as crude prices have been climbing amid increasing tensions between the United States and Iran.

U.S. crude prices settled above $100/bbl for the first time in more than a month Friday, much higher than the $86/bbl executives point to as the price needed to profitably drill new wells.

data.title: Developers to Pay $160 Million for Palm Beach Mansion They Plan to Tear Down — WSJ
data.description:
By Katherine Clarke

An oceanfront estate in Palm Beach, Fla., is in contract to be sold for about $160 million, according to the developer Todd Michael Glaser, who is one of the buyers.

If it closes, the deal would be one of the priciest ever in Palm Beach, where the record for a single-family home sale is held by a $170 million purchase by luxury car dealer Michael Cantanucci. The Florida price record was set last year by the sale of a home in Naples for $225 million.

Glaser, along with developer David Edelstein of TriCap, is purchasing the longtime home of the late real-estate developer Murray Goodman and his wife, Joanie Goodman. The deal is effectively a land play: The pink-hued, circa-1980s Goodman compound is in good condition, but Glaser said he and Edelstein plan to raze it and potentially build two separate homes on the roughly 2-acre site. The deal is contingent on the sellers splitting the property into two tax lots so they can be developed separately, said Glaser, who added that dividing the lot is the best way to capitalize on the velocity in the ultra-high-end market.

In Palm Beach, it isn't unusual for large oceanfront lots to be subdivided. An estate known as Maison de L'Amitié, once owned by President Trump, was subdivided by the Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev and split into three separate oceanfront lots, for instance.

The Goodman property first came on the market for $185 million in November 2025. Murray, who was known for the development of Palm Beach landmarks like the Esplanade luxury fashion center on Worth Avenue, died in 2024 aged 99, and Joanie was looking to downsize, their daughter, Marley Overman, said last year. Overman wasn't immediately available for comment on the prospective sale.

The compound was built on the site of what was once one of South Florida's most famous homes: Playa Riente, a 1920s-era mansion demolished in the 1950s by Anna Dodge, widow of automaker Horace Dodge. The Goodmans purchased the land for the house in the mid-1970s.

The home spans about 18,000 square feet, with 12 bedrooms spread across the main house and guesthouse.

Glaser is known for developing and renovating ultraluxury homes. A property he redeveloped on Tarpon Island in Palm Beach sold for about $150 million in 2024. He's also developing a Miami Beach megamansion on a site he bought for $105 million last year.

Overman, a real-estate agent at Illustrated Properties, had the listing with Gary Pohrer of Serhant. Spencer Schlager of Douglas Elliman represented Glaser.

The deal is the latest $100 million-plus teardown for Palm Beach.

Write to Katherine Clarke at Katherine.Clarke@wsj.com

data.title: Oracle Stocks Edge Up as $1 Billion Backs AI Partners
data.description:
Enterprise-software provider Oracle committed $1 billion over four years to strengthen its partner network, with shares trading at $125.95, up 0.33%, at 10:35 a.m. ET on Friday. The money will support training, technical resources, cloud migrations and sales efforts. The business logic is straightforward: help more partners get customers onto Oracle's platforms and keep them spending.

There is plenty of demand to serve. Oracle's fiscal first-quarter results showed revenue rising 30% to $19.3 billion, with cloud infrastructure revenue jumping 121% to $7.4 billion. Total cloud revenue reached $11.6 billion, up 62%, while remaining performance obligations stood at $664 billion. The challenge is execution: signed commitments still need to become delivered services and recognized revenue.

The financial profile shows that tension: Oracle's GF Score of 88/100 pairs strong growth and profitability readings with weaker financial strength and valuation readings. Partner support could expand implementation capacity without Oracle handling every deployment itself. But spending is the starting line. Investors should watch whether the incentives bring additional cloud usage, faster migrations and better conversion of contracted business into revenue.

data.title: Hop-on's Digitalage Targets Enterprise Licensing for AI-Assisted Moderation Technology
data.description:
Former Nokia licensing executive Robert T. Braun joins industry leaders at IAM Live as Digitalage prepares its first enterprise-licensing candidate and creator-platform launch

TEMECULA, CA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Hop-on, Inc. today identified AI-assisted text moderation as the first technology its wholly owned subsidiary, Digitalage, Inc., is preparing for enterprise evaluation and potential licensing. The initiative outlines a second prospective commercialization channel alongside Digitalage's creator-facing media platform.

Digitalage's strategy is to operate its underlying media infrastructure within its creator ecosystem while preparing selected technologies for licensing to outside platforms, developers and enterprises through APIs and negotiated commercial agreements.

The announcement follows Digitalage Chief Executive Officer Robert T. Braun's participation at IAM Live: Patent Transactions 2026, held October 22 in San Diego.

The event marked Braun's first IAM appearance representing Digitalage as CEO following his appointment in September 2026. Braun and Hop-on Chairman and CEO Peter Michaels also held preliminary discussions with industry participants regarding technology licensing, intellectual-property commercialization and potential strategic relationships. No agreements were announced.

"Digitalage was created for creators, but not as a one-use system," said Peter Michaels, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Hop-on and Founder and Chairman of Digitalage. "The infrastructure we're developing to manage, protect and monetize digital media is designed to serve businesses well beyond our own creator ecosystem. Our objective is to build it, prove it and turn the components that solve real problems into commercial opportunities."

AI-Assisted Moderation: First Enterprise Licensing Priority

Digitalage's initial enterprise licensing candidate is an AI-assisted text-moderation engine designed to analyze live chat, comments and creator interactions, identifying content that warrants review.

The company is developing optimized AI models and API integration capabilities intended to allow organizations to incorporate moderation into their existing applications and operational workflows.

The technology is approaching demonstration readiness. Near-term priorities are completing the demonstration, validating operating performance and evaluating integration requirements with prospective pilot partners. Digitalage welcomes inquiries from organizations interested in exploring potential pilot deployments.

Additional capabilities under development and evaluation include visual and video content protection, live-media infrastructure and digital rights-management workflows.

Robert Braun: Turning Intellectual Property Into Commercial Value

At IAM Live, Braun participated in the session "SEP Licensing Strategies That Maximise Returns" alongside Kent Baker, IP Adviser at TRASNA, and Roberto Ribeiro, Partner at DANIEL.

The discussion addressed licensing negotiations, cross-industry standard-essential patent disputes and fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory (FRAND) licensing structures.

Braun brings more than 20 years of international intellectual-property licensing experience, including nearly 12 years at Nokia, where he led patent-licensing strategy across the Americas and portions of Asia.

Digitalage's enterprise initiative concerns its own media technologies and associated intellectual-property rights.

"Licensing starts with identifying a problem worth solving and demonstrating that your technology delivers value," said Braun. "Digitalage is developing capabilities with applications beyond our own platform. Our priority is to validate those technologies, protect the underlying rights and build commercial relationships that can create long-term value."

Creator Launch and Enterprise Commercialization

Digitalage continues to advance its creator-facing platform, including live broadcasting, paid viewer access, replays, content libraries, creator controls and monetization.

As announced October 21, the company is targeting an expanded creator Alpha in November, broader Beta testing in early December and commercial availability in the United States, Canada and Mexico before December 31, 2026.

Digitalage's creator ecosystem is intended to provide a real-world operating environment for its infrastructure. The company's next major operational objective is to validate the complete paid-media transaction workflow, from live broadcast and viewer purchase through replay availability and accurate creator settlement.

The launch remains dependent on successful testing, financing, payment readiness and applicable approvals.

Digitalage's enterprise licensing initiative complements these activities by creating an additional potential revenue opportunity from selected components of the company's underlying technology.

Future commercial arrangements will depend on technology validation, applicable intellectual-property rights and definitive agreements. No licensing revenue is being announced in connection with the IAM event.

About Hop-on, Inc. and Digitalage

Hop-on, Inc. is a publicly traded technology company and parent of Digitalage, Inc.

Digitalage is developing AI-assisted media infrastructure for live and recorded content, creator monetization, content moderation, verification, rights management and distribution. Its technology strategy centers on connecting digital content with its identity, permissions, ownership information and commercial rights.

Digitalage: Ingest → Protect → Monetize.

Disclaimer

Forward-Looking Statements

This release contains forward-looking statements concerning Digitalage's enterprise licensing strategy, technology development, demonstration readiness, potential pilot programs, commercial partnerships, intellectual-property rights, creator onboarding, strategic discussions and anticipated commercial launch.

Actual results may differ materially due to engineering and testing outcomes, financing availability, intellectual-property protection, third-party dependencies, payment-processing readiness, regulatory requirements, commercial negotiations, competition and market adoption. Potential licensing opportunities may not result in agreements or revenue, and planned launch dates may change.

Hop-on undertakes no obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by applicable law.

data.title: IBM Stocks Weigh Cash Allocation After Software Earnings Improve
data.description:
Enterprise software and consulting company IBM edged down 0.87% to $249.91 at 10:29 a.m. ET Friday, with its latest earnings putting cash allocation in focus. Software growth has momentum. The spending bill is hefty, too: acquisitions consumed $11.4 billion through September, compared with $7.8 billion in free cash flow. Friday's Motley Fool review revisited the software performance, but investors also have a balance sheet to weigh.

IBM's quarterly results showed software revenue of $7.8 billion, up 9% at constant currencies, while consulting grew 2% on the same basis. Free cash flow reached $3 billion, rising $700 million from a year earlier. That covered $1.6 billion in dividends roughly 1.9 times, leaving $1.4 billion before acquisitions and other financing demands. Total debt, including financing debt, stood at $63.8 billion. The business is generating more cash. Management still has competing uses for it.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a GF Score of 76/100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 21.31, with profitability stronger than financial strengtha useful reminder that earnings quality and balance-sheet capacity deserve separate scrutiny. The next test is execution: acquisitions need to contribute, consulting needs to build momentum, and stronger software sales need to keep converting into cash. Growth gets attention. Funding it well determines how much shareholders keep.

data.title: Lam Research Stocks Edge Lower as $8.6 Billion Guidance Tests Shipment Capacity
data.description:
Semiconductor equipment supplier Lam Research traded at $228.28, down 0.81%, at 10:25 a.m. ET on October 23 as attention shifted from September's record results to December's delivery targets. A strong quarter only carries so much weight when investors want the next one to impress. Investor's Business Daily reported that September earnings beat expectations modestly, while December guidance merely matched estimates.

Lam's results showed September revenue of $8.219 billion and a 40.0% GAAP operating margin, with customer support-related revenue and other sales contributing $2.487 billion. December revenue guidance stands at $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, alongside a 40.5% GAAP operating margin midpoint. That revenue target implies roughly 4.6% sequential growth after September's 22% increase. Growth is slowing against a much bigger base; that alone does not establish weaker demand.

The next test is execution: deliver the revenue while protecting margins. Deferred revenue reached $2.66 billion, although recognizing that revenue depends on the relevant contractual requirements being met. GuruFocus's snapshot pairs a 97/100 GF Score with a 33.98 price-to-earnings ratio, suggesting strong business fundamentals come with substantial earnings expectations. Lam has delivered the record quarter. Now it needs to deliver the follow-through.

data.title: Corn Settles Lower in Lackluster Grains Trade — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Kirk Maltais

  • Corn for December delivery falls 1% on the Chicago Board of Trade at $4.56 a bushel as funds continue to unload long positions.
  • Soybeans for November delivery rise 0.3% to $12.56 1/2 a bushel.
  • Wheat for December delivery settles little changed at $6.25 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Unwinding in Process: Managed money is continuing its gradual shift from being record long to building short positions, said Brady Huck of EmpowerAg Trading. "It's been another bruising week in the grain markets, [as] fund selling pressure continued to weigh heavy on the grains," he said.

Traders may be looking for a turnaround in corn specifically, as an unwinding of a mountain of long positions in corn may be soon completed.

Black Sea Woes: Fighting appears to be escalating again in the Black Sea, which gave wheat futures some support in Europe as new strikes were reported overnight. Support appears limited now though, as the most active contract ends flat.

"There were no substantial results that would have given rise to hopes of an end to Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine," Commerzbank said in a note.

INSIGHT

Quick to Sell: Farmers have been seen aggressively selling their harvests when CBOT grain futures climbed back up to recent highs in the late summer/early fall.

That may have created other issues further down the supply chain, said Tanner Ehmke of CoBank in a note.

"Farmers have been aggressive sellers during recent rallies in corn, soybeans and wheat, transferring ownership of grain to elevators and cooperatives earlier than usual," he said.

Focus on Demand: Ahead of next month's WASDE, traders are keeping a close eye on what demand indicators show for U.S. grain exports.

"Our focus remains on demand rather than supply," said Rich Nelson of Allendale Inc. For corn and soybeans, export sales are a key metric, while for wheat "psychological pressure" from the Russia-Ukraine talks is seen having more impact even with little progress in those talks, he added.

AHEAD

  • The USDA is scheduled to release its weekly Grain Export Inspections Report at 11 a.m. EDT Monday.
  • The USDA is due to release its weekly Crop Progress Report at 4 p.m. EDT Monday.
  • Smithfield Foods is scheduled to release its 3Q earnings report at 4:30 a.m. EDT Tuesday.
  • The EIA is due to release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update Report at 10:30 a.m. EDT Wednesday.
  • Pilgrims Pride is scheduled to release its 3Q earnings report after the stock market closes on Wednesday.

data.title: Lawyers gird for congressional probes if Democrats take control
data.description:
By David Thomas and Sara Merken

A Democratic takeover of at least one chamber of Congress following next month's midterm elections could be a boon to law firms angling for roles in a potential surge of congressional investigations.

Several lawyers and lobbyists in Washington said they're communicating with current and potential clients in anticipation of a spate of new probes on Capitol Hill if Democrats tip the balance. Reuters has reported that Democrats are widely expected to win control of the House, though the Senate is too close to call.

Anyone ignoring inquiries from Democratic lawmakers risks the chance they could have subpoena power in the next Congress, said Brian Pomper, who co-leads Akin Gump's lobbying and public policy practice.

"They should really be preparing now," Pomper said.

After two years in the minority during Republican President Donald Trump's first term, newly-empowered Democrats could scrutinize a range of targets, from administration figures to corporate donors and participants in business deals brokered by the Trump family. Unlike the White House, private companies cannot claim that their activities are protected by executive privilege.

Democrats are "telegraphing that they’re going to go towards companies for information" because the administration will not cooperate, said Susanne Sachsman Grooms, the leader of Cooley's congressional investigations practice.

Grooms said she is planning to meet with a small group of clients at private dinners in New York and San Francisco after the election to discuss the results and their implications.

US law firm Brownstein Hyatt launched a website to track investigative activity, said Will Moschella, who co-chairs the firm's government relations department, and posted hundreds of letters Democratic lawmakers in the US House and Senate have sent since last year that could augur future probes.

Lawyers at several firms said they expanded their congressional investigations practices over the past year, while others are still hiring.

In March, Akin Gump hired Marcus Childress, a former senior adviser to US Representative Jamie Raskin, the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee and a Democrat. Last month, Cooley brought Jessica Donlon, who has served as general counsel to Republican US Representatives Brett Guthrie and James Comer.

Aaron Cutler, who leads Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's government relations practice, said he has been given a mandate to hire more people.

"We've been busy all year," Cutler said. "We're expecting to be busier next year."

LOBBYING REVENUES ON THE RISE – AGAIN

Several firms reported record-setting US lobbying revenues once again in the third quarter, as lobbyists also look ahead to the post-election landscape.

Florida-founded lobbying ​firm Ballard Partners said it brought in $35.01 million in its best-ever quarter, 39.6% more than the same time period last year. The firm, which previously employed former US Attorney General Pam Bondi, has seen massive revenue growth since President Donald Trump took office last year.

Law firms Brownstein Hyatt, Akin Gump and Squire Patton Boggs reported federal lobbying revenues of $22.5 million, $18.85 million and $7.9 million, respectively, while lobbying firms BGR Group and Cornerstone Government Affairs reported $22.5 million and $15.6 million. Representatives from those five firms said these are new quarterly records.

Akin Gump said lobbying on trade and tariff issues was a major driver, while Brownstein Hyatt cited a range of areas including healthcare and tax.

Lobbyists are required to report quarterly revenue under the federal Lobbying Disclosure Act.

Not every firm saw an increase. Hogan Lovells Cadwalader said its federal lobbying revenue in the third quarter dropped to $2.97 million from $3.7 million in the prior quarter. K&L Gates reported a quarterly decline from $5.5 million to $4.8 million.

Aaron Cutler, the leader of Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's government relations practice, said in a statement the firm has "continued to see an increase in non-LDA work," including congressional investigations and its work for foreign clients like Venezuela.

Karishma Shah Page, who co-leads K&L Gates' public policy and law practice, said in an email that there was heavy preparation underway ahead of the election, and that she expects both the end of the year and the next congressional session to be busy. She noted that the third quarter tends to be slower prior to a midterm election, and that Congress spent limited time in session in July and September.

Federal lobbying spending has continually increased ​since 2016, surpassing $5 billion last year, according to nonprofit ​research group OpenSecrets. As of July 23, companies, trade ⁠groups and other entities have spent $2.74 billion this year, per OpenSecrets.

COOLEY MATCHES MILBANK SALARY SCALE

Cooley will raise salaries for its US associates in January, aligning with the associate compensation scale that rival firm Milbank rolled out earlier this year.

Associates at Palo Alto-founded Cooley will have base salaries ranging from $235,000 to $455,000, depending on seniority, according to an internal Cooley memo published by the website Above the Law. The firm will also hand out “special” bonuses for the year to eligible associates, the memo said, without specifying the amounts.

Large US firms have largely stayed quiet since Milbank announced salary increases in June, though McDermott, Will & Schulte was among a handful of firms that matched the new scale. Milbank, which in recent years has been a first mover among large firms on associate compensation, also rolled out so-called special bonuses of up to $25,000 in July.

data.title: Canadian dollar hits five-week high as data supports rate hike bets
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar strengthened to a five-week high against its US counterpart on Friday as oil prices rose and domestic retail sales data supported expectations the Bank of Canada would raise interest rates next week.

The loonie was trading 0.1% higher at 1.40 per US dollar, or 71.43 US cents, after touching its strongest intraday level since September 16 at 1.3969.

  • It left the currency on track for a seventh straight day of gains, which would be the longest daily winning streak since March 2022.

  • For the week, the currency was up 1% — heading for its biggest weekly advance since April.

  • Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% in August from July, led by higher sales at motor vehicle and parts dealers, while a preliminary estimate showed sales increasing by 0.7% in September.

  • "Given the resilience in these spending numbers, we still believe the Bank of Canada is headed for a rate increase next week," Oskar Stone, an analyst at Desjardins, said in a note, adding that the data points to third-quarter GDP growth of 2%.

  • The Bank of Canada will raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.

  • Investors see a roughly 80% chance the BoC hikes next week. Bets on a hike have increased in recent days after hawkish comments from Governor Tiff Macklem and as Alberta voted by a large majority to remain part of Canada. (0#CADIRPR)

  • The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, rose after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East. US crude oil futures settled 3.8% higher at $103.27 a barrel.

  • Canadian bond yields rose across the curve, tracking moves in US Treasuries. The 10-year (CA10YT=RR) was up 5.1 basis points at 3.838%.

data.title: CO2NNEX(R) Digital Platform for Integrated Management of the Environmental Value of Sustainable Liquid Fuel (HVO) to Commence Operation in Demonstration of Sustainable Fuels Certificates Scheme
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Osaka Gas Co., Ltd. ("Osaka Gas") and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. ("MHI") today commenced operation of CO2NNEX?(1), a digital platform jointly developed and deployed by the two companies, under the 2026 Project for the Establishment of Environmental Value Certification Scheme, etc. (Demonstration Project for Consideration of the Building of a Scheme for Certification and Transfer of Environmental Value of Sustainable Fuels) implemented by the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan ("ANRE") (hereinafter referred to as "the Scheme Demonstration")(2). In the Scheme Demonstration, CO2NNEX will be used in consideration of the system requirements needed for the processes of issuing, transferring, and retiring sustainable fuel certificates.

Toward the widespread deployment of sustainable fuels (e-gasoline, SAF, HVO(3), e-methane, biogas, etc.), the adoption of sustainable fuels certificates scheme to certify and manage the environmental value of those fuels is being considered. The Scheme Demonstration is being conducted to examine issues in the adoption and the design of this scheme.

Osaka Gas and MHI aim to create value in the following forms through CO2NNEX, with a view to the widespread deployment of Sustainable liquid fuels and full-scale operation of the system in the future.

(1) Realization of digitalization and operational efficiency improvement for procedures, including collaboration with third-party certification bodies

Exchange of information between applicants and third-party certification bodies for procedures such as application, verification, and issuing of certificates will be completed on CO2NNEX. The introduction of a digital platform will enable the building of processes for prompt verification and issuance of certificates, minimizing the workload involved in procedures such as document handling. It will also enable reliable management of certificates without manual operations as the results of the digital authorization performed by the third-party certification bodies will be automatically reflected in transfer, retirement, and management processes after the certificates are issued on the system.

(2) Prevention of double-counting, enabling appropriate management and enhanced reliability of environmental value A mechanism to prevent double-counting of environmental value through the use of digital trust technology will be built into the system. System requirements will also be organized with the aim of contributing to a highly reliable certificate system design that will ensure traceability.

ANRE is also conducting a demonstration of a sustainable fuels certificates scheme for e-methane and biogas in the area of utility gas. Osaka Gas and MHI are making considerations for the use of CO2NNEX by the parties involved in that demonstration for e-methane and biogas. Going forward, Osaka Gas and MHI will contribute to the practical application of various sustainable fuels through the building and provision of system requirements with a high level of utility and reliability to meet the needs of future social infrastructure in the areas of both gas and liquid fuels.

(1) CO2NNEX:

CO2NNEX is a digital platform developed by MHI for the visualization and management of CO2 supply chain. In the Scheme Demonstration, Osaka Gas and MHI will use CO2NNEX to jointly consider the system requirements needed for the operational processes for issuing, transferring, and retiring sustainable fuels certificates. This system also has functions for transfer and management of attribute data for clean gas certificates used to certify the environmental value of e-methane and biogas, which have been used for purposes such as Expo 2025 and Nagaoka Methanation Demonstration."CO2NNEX" is a registered trademark of MHI in Japan and other countries.

For details, see the following press release:

"Operations Started for the Nagaoka Methanation Demonstration Utilizing the CO2NNEX? Digital Platform for Transfer and Management of e-Methane Clean Gas Certificates" (June 4, 2026)

data.title: Seaport Research Issues Stark Nvidia Warning on Nvidia Stock
data.description:
Nvidia faces mounting competitive pressure and potential financial risks from its growing investment commitments, according to Seaport Research, which maintained its Sell rating on the chipmaker and a $180 price target.

Analyst Jay Goldberg said Nvidia's financing arrangements may reflect rising pressure from rivals. He also questioned whether the company's efforts to support customers and secure supplies could create competing demands on its financial resources.

Nvidia added roughly $250 billion in commitments during its latest quarter, according to Goldberg. Those obligations include spending to secure components and support data center construction, tying the company more closely to the expansion of AI infrastructure.

Goldberg also highlighted a separate financing initiative involving Nvidia, six private equity firms and banks. The proposed platform could provide about $500 billion in funding, with the possibility of reaching $1 trillion. Nvidia would not bear the entire obligation, but the analyst views its role as central to the arrangement.

The concern is that financing structures built to accelerate growth could magnify losses if demand for computing capacity weakens. Goldberg warned that infrastructure providers reliant on Nvidia's support could face pressure during a downturn, potentially adding strain when the chipmaker's own sales and cash flow soften.

data.title: Treasury Yields Rise, Eurozone Bond Yields Fall Amid French Concerns — WSJ
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields rose Friday but remained near the previous day's lows as investors sought safety from the turmoil in French government bonds ahead of a closely watched interest-rate decision.

The Federal Reserve is expected to keep rates on hold Wednesday and resume a hiking cycle in December, as sticky inflation weighs on consumer sentiment while economic activity remains resilient.

The 10-year Treasury yield on Friday traded at 4.992%, slightly up from the day before but on pace for a weekly decline, according to Tradeweb.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
